field.label: Refresh (seconds)
field.help: How often the map reads the state table for the live traffic. Shorter is smoother but asks more of the firewall; 10 seconds suits most networks.

field.label: Hidden networks
field.help: Interface names (for example opt5) of networks the map should not show. They can still be shown with the network chips.

field.label: Flag new devices
field.help: Mark devices that were never approved as new, with Approve and Ban buttons.

field.label: Firewall actions
field.help: Show Ban, Block Internet, schedules, port forwards and the rule switches in the device panel. Untick for a read-only map; the changes always use the privileges of the logged-in user.

field.label: Port scans
field.help: Show the Quick and Full scan buttons (nmap on the firewall). Results already stored stay visible.

field.label: Use AdGuard Home
field.help: Show the domains each device asks for, the ones AdGuard blocked, and a button to block DNS for a device (AdGuard "disallowed clients").

field.label: Host
field.help: Where the AdGuard Home web interface runs, as seen from the firewall. When AdGuard Home runs on this firewall (os-adguardhome-maxit) use 127.0.0.1.

field.label: Port
field.help: Port of the AdGuard Home web interface: the one in its address bar, for example 3000 in http://10.0.1.1:3000. 3000 is the AdGuard Home default; it is not the DNS port 53.

field.label: HTTPS
field.help: Tick when the AdGuard Home web interface is opened with https://.

field.label: User name
field.help: An AdGuard Home user. Stored in the firewall configuration.

field.label: Verify certificate
field.help: Check the certificate of AdGuard Home when HTTPS is ticked. Leave it off for a self-signed certificate.
